title: Fermion-doubling problem in Chiral discretizations of Quantum field theory: Definitive proof, Fixing, and Computation of two-point correlation function
abstract: We give the definitive proof that the Dirac Quantum Cellular Automaton (QCA) used for both quantum simulation and algorithmic foundations of Quantum Field Theory (QFT), and especially of Quantum Electrodynamics (QED), as put forward in References https://doi.org/10.1007/s11128-019-2555-4 and https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2023-11-08-1179, does exhibit Fermion Doubling (FD), albeit thrice as less severe as discrete-time standard Lattice Gauge Theories (LGTs) -- as shown in Reference arXiv:2505.07900 -- , which are naive regarding the spacetime discretization of differential operators acting on fermionic fields. The proof is done for the $(1 + 1)$D Dirac-QCA model. We show that the (one-time-step) two-point correlation function, also called Green's function (GF), of the Dirac QCA, is of astonishing simplicity, which is in contrast with the GF of the Dirac equation. We also compare, both qualitatively and quantitatively, this Dirac QCA to the continuous-time-LGT spatial discretization of Dirac fermions regarding how well these two lattice models approximate their naive continuum limit -- which is nothing but the Dirac equation -- even when far away from that limit, a situation which must be considered because of experimental limitations in quantum simulation -- : the Dirac QCA is better for ultrarelativistic regimes, whereas continuous-time LGT is better for non-relativistic regimes. In a second part of this work, we compute the GF of the FD-fixed model put forward in the last cited reference, called Flavored Dirac QCA (FQCA) -- which staggers an extra, artificial flavor \emph{only}, on a diamond spacetime lattice, and does not stagger chirality as staggered fermions in usual LGT. The structure of this FQCA two-point correlation function is of extreme simplicity, and can be expressed in a very simple manner in terms of the four chiral components of the FD-suffering, original-model GF.
summary: This paper tackles the persistent Fermion-Doubling problem in chiral QFT discretizations by analyzing the Dirac Quantum Cellular Automaton (QCA). It proves that while FD exists, the QCA offers a superior approximation to the continuum limit in ultrarelativistic regimes compared to standard LGTs. The authors provide explicit calculations for the Green's functions of both the original and fixed models.
main_problem: The paper definitively proves that the Dirac Quantum Cellular Automaton (QCA) exhibits Fermion Doubling (FD) in its chiral discretization, and compares its approximation quality to continuous-time Lattice Gauge Theories (LGTs). It also computes the Green's function for a fixed version of this model.
main_result: The QCA is shown to be superior to continuous-time LGTs for describing ultrarelativistic regimes, while the latter performs better in non-relativistic ones. The resulting two-point correlation functions are found to possess an 'astonishing simplicity'.
method: The analysis involves rigorous mathematical proofs, calculating one-time-step two-point correlation functions (Green's functions) using both direct and Fourier space methods, and performing systematic comparisons between lattice approximations and the continuum Dirac equation.
model_or_system: The primary model is the $(1+1)$D Dirac Quantum Cellular Automaton (QCA), which serves as a discrete spacetime discretization for QFT like QED. It is compared against continuous-time LGTs and an advanced, FD-fixed variant called Flavored Dirac QCA (FQCA).
key_observables: The one-time-step two-point correlation function (Green's function, GF) of the Dirac QCA and FQCA; comparison metrics for approximating the continuum Dirac equation.
important_parameters: Energy regimes (ultrarelativistic vs. non-relativistic); lattice spacing ($\epsilon$); momentum ($p$) and energy ($E$).
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on the single-particle sector (free models) when studying and fixing FD, although comparisons are made to experimental limitations in quantum simulation.
figures_summary: Figures compare ratios of matrix elements for different lattice models across momentum space, illustrating performance differences between regimes.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first proving the existence and nature of FD in the Dirac QCA. It then quantitatively compares the QCA to continuous-time LGTs regarding their approximation quality in specific energy regimes. Finally, it computes the GF for the specialized FQCA model.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides rigorous theoretical benchmarks for lattice discretizations of fundamental quantum field theories, which are crucial for developing and interpreting results from quantum simulation platforms.
